Summary: Establish reliable TMDB movie data ingestion
Description: Deliver a repeatable and observable acquisition path from TMDB into the raw movie catalog. Scope covers credentials, API behavior, persisted output, and failure handling.
Acceptance Criteria: Raw movie payloads are persisted in the agreed schema; transient and permanent API failures are distinguishable; no credentials are committed.

Summary: Configure TMDB credentials and extraction inputs
Description: Read the API credential from environment configuration and validate extraction range and output path before network calls.
Acceptance Criteria: Missing credentials or invalid ranges produce an explicit actionable error; valid settings are used without exposing the credential in logs.

Summary: Make TMDB extraction resilient and rate-limit aware
Description: Handle request timeouts, HTTP errors, 429 responses, and retry delays explicitly; preserve progress and continue only for documented recoverable cases.
Acceptance Criteria: 429 and transient failures use bounded backoff; non-retryable errors are reported; failed movie IDs are observable; extraction completes without silently swallowing unexpected exceptions.

Summary: Validate and persist the raw TMDB response contract
Description: Check that the fetched response contains the fields required downstream and write valid JSON atomically with extraction metadata.
Acceptance Criteria: Raw output is valid UTF-8 JSON with metadata and movie records; malformed responses are counted and reported; partial output is not presented as a successful complete run.

Summary: Support resumable extraction runs
Description: Record completed and failed IDs so an interrupted range can be retried without refetching all successful records.
Acceptance Criteria: Restarting a run can resume from recorded progress; duplicate movie IDs are not introduced; resume state is documented and can be safely reset.

Summary: Create a validated and analysis-ready movie dataset
Description: Turn raw API records into consistent processed data with explicit schema, duplicate handling, null policies, and validation.
Acceptance Criteria: Clean output follows a documented schema; invalid records and transformations are measured; automated tests cover data quality rules.

Summary: Define the canonical movie dataset schema
Description: Document required and optional movie fields, types, nullability, list-valued fields, and output formats used by the pipeline.
Acceptance Criteria: Schema matches fields produced by extraction and consumed downstream; required-field failures are explicit; schema documentation includes types and null policy.

Summary: Make cleaning transformations null-safe and deterministic
Description: Harden genre and keyword normalization, duplicate removal, date conversion, numeric coercion, and output directory creation for missing or malformed values.
Acceptance Criteria: Cleaning handles absent optional columns and null or malformed nested values without crashing; repeated runs produce equivalent results; duplicate movie IDs are removed.

Summary: Apply and document missing-value and range policies
Description: Specify per-field handling for runtime, budget, revenue, ratings, and dates; report records changed or excluded by each rule.
Acceptance Criteria: Policies are documented and tested; invalid runtime and out-of-range values are handled consistently; imputations do not silently change unrelated columns.

Summary: Add automated tests for extraction cleaning and validation
Description: Create unit tests with small fixture datasets covering valid, empty, malformed, duplicate, missing, and boundary-value records.
Acceptance Criteria: Tests run offline without TMDB credentials or a live MongoDB service; all defined data rules have positive and negative test cases.

Summary: Prepare and persist reusable movie features
Description: Generate consistent date, genre, keyword, budget, popularity, and engagement features and store catalog records reproducibly in MongoDB.
Acceptance Criteria: Feature generation has a tested input/output contract; MongoDB configuration is environment based; repeated pipeline runs do not leave duplicate or stale records.

Summary: Make feature generation robust to incomplete catalog fields
Description: Guard date parsing, null genre and keyword values, invalid numeric data, and bin boundaries in feature engineering.
Acceptance Criteria: Feature generation succeeds on valid cleaned fixtures with optional values missing; output feature columns and types are documented and stable.

Summary: Externalize and verify MongoDB connection settings
Description: Read the MongoDB URI and database/collection names from environment configuration and provide clear connection failure reporting.
Acceptance Criteria: Local and container deployments use configuration rather than hard-coded credentials; invalid connection settings fail clearly; secrets are absent from logs and source.

Summary: Make MongoDB catalog loads idempotent
Description: Replace delete-all then insert behavior with an upsert or staging-and-swap strategy keyed by movie_id, with duplicate and empty-input safeguards.
Acceptance Criteria: Re-running the same load yields one record per movie ID; a failed load does not silently erase the previous good catalog; empty input is rejected and reported.

Summary: Verify stored catalog against the canonical schema
Description: Add post-load counts and required-field checks and expose clear success/failure details to the pipeline.
Acceptance Criteria: Load result count matches accepted input count; duplicate IDs and required-field violations are reported; verification failure makes the task fail.

Summary: Deliver a validated audience-engagement classifier
Description: Train, compare, save, and serve a reproducible high-engagement model with leakage-safe evaluation and documented metrics.
Acceptance Criteria: Target definition and evaluation are documented; model selection uses validation data only; saved model loads and predicts using the same feature contract.

Summary: Define the high-engagement target and prevent leakage
Description: Confirm the vote-count quantile target and exclude target-derived or post-outcome fields from model inputs before any fitting.
Acceptance Criteria: Target threshold is calculated from training data only; target and leakage-prone fields are excluded from predictors; class balance and target definition are recorded.

Summary: Build reproducible classification evaluation
Description: Compare the supported classifiers with stratified train/test and cross-validation; report precision, recall, F1, ROC-AUC, and confusion matrices.
Acceptance Criteria: All models use consistent splits and metrics; random seeds and fold strategy are fixed; metrics are saved or reproducibly emitted; selection criterion is explicit.

Summary: Select and serialize the validated classifier bundle
Description: Choose the best validated model, refit only after selection, and persist the estimator with feature metadata and version information.
Acceptance Criteria: Model artifact is written to the documented path; it can be loaded in a clean process; bundle includes model name and feature/target metadata; failed training does not overwrite a valid artifact.

Summary: Add prediction contract and model smoke tests
Description: Validate expected input columns and output probabilities and add a smoke test using a saved or fixture model artifact.
Acceptance Criteria: Known valid input yields finite predictions with documented output shape; missing required inputs produce a clear error; test does not retrain the full model.

Summary: Make movie clustering interpretable and repeatable
Description: Produce meaningful movie groups, select cluster count with a documented metric, and expose cluster profiles and representatives.
Acceptance Criteria: Cluster selection and feature inputs are reproducible; results include interpretable profiles and representative movies; low-data edge cases are handled.

Summary: Stabilize clustering preprocessing and candidate selection
Description: Reuse a documented feature pipeline, handle sparse and missing inputs, and validate eligible cluster counts before fitting K-Means.
Acceptance Criteria: Repeated runs with the same data and seed yield consistent results; invalid candidate cluster counts are skipped or rejected explicitly; silhouette scoring is only performed when mathematically valid.

Summary: Generate cluster profiles and representative movies
Description: Calculate cluster sizes, key numeric summaries, common genres and keywords, and nearest representative titles from fitted assignments.
Acceptance Criteria: Each non-empty cluster has a summary and representative titles; missing profile columns do not crash the report; outputs identify cluster IDs.

Summary: Provide content-based movie recommendations
Description: Build and serve TF-IDF recommendations from movie overviews with robust handling for empty text, unknown terms, and ranking ties.
Acceptance Criteria: Recommender artifacts are generated from the current catalog; queries return deterministic relevant titles; empty or out-of-vocabulary inputs show helpful guidance.

Summary: Build versioned TF-IDF recommendation artifacts
Description: Clean overview text, exclude unusable records, fit the vectorizer, and persist aligned movie metadata and sparse vectors.
Acceptance Criteria: Vectorizer, sparse matrix, and movie rows have identical ordering and compatible dimensions; empty overview rows are excluded and counted; artifacts are written to documented paths.

Summary: Implement robust recommendation ranking and limits
Description: Rank positive cosine-similarity results, handle empty query vectors and empty catalogs, and ensure returned results respect the requested limit.
Acceptance Criteria: Results are ordered by descending similarity; no-match and unusable-query cases return explicit user feedback; result count never exceeds configured limit.

Summary: Test recommendation relevance and artifact compatibility
Description: Add tests for text cleanup, exact/partial matches, no vocabulary match, empty catalog, ranking order, and stale or incompatible artifacts.
Acceptance Criteria: Offline tests verify ranking and edge cases; incompatible artifact shapes raise a clear error; test fixtures do not require a live database.

Summary: Deliver the CineMind analytics dashboard
Description: Present the catalog overview, engagement predictions, on-demand clusters, and content recommendations in a usable Streamlit experience.
Acceptance Criteria: Core dashboard workflows work from documented data sources; filters and user inputs are validated; unavailable data or models are explained without crashing.

Summary: Complete catalog overview and filter experience
Description: Show key catalog metrics and existing visualizations with genre, release-year, and minimum-rating filters applied consistently to the table and charts.
Acceptance Criteria: Filters update visible catalog results consistently; empty filter results show a clear empty state; missing optional fields do not crash the overview.

Summary: Integrate classifier and explain prediction results
Description: Allow selecting a movie and display its high-engagement prediction/score with a clear explanation of what the score represents.
Acceptance Criteria: Prediction uses the saved model bundle and expected feature columns; absent model artifact gives actionable guidance; invalid selection is handled safely.

Summary: Integrate clustering workflow and readable results
Description: Run clustering on demand and display cluster sizes, profiles, map, and representative titles with progress or failure feedback.
Acceptance Criteria: User can trigger a cluster run; output includes summaries and representative titles; too-small or invalid catalogs show a clear message.

Summary: Integrate movie-based content recommendations
Description: Let a user choose or search a seed movie and show ranked recommendations with match scores and a no-results state.
Acceptance Criteria: Recommendations render in descending score order; unavailable artifacts and no matches are explained; selected seed movie is excluded from its own recommendations.

Summary: Add dashboard loading and error states
Description: Handle missing MongoDB, unavailable model artifacts, malformed catalog records, and refresh failures with explicit status messages and safe recovery.
Acceptance Criteria: Each required service failure is visible and actionable; refresh does not leave stale success messaging; healthy fallback data sources are clearly identified.

Summary: Automate and release the end-to-end product safely
Description: Make the Airflow workflow, local containers, automated checks, and documentation reliable enough for repeatable development and handoff.
Acceptance Criteria: Pipeline dependencies reflect data flow; container startup and health are verifiable; tests and operational instructions support a clean setup.

Summary: Align Airflow task dependencies and artifact contracts
Description: Verify extraction, cleaning, feature engineering, MongoDB load, classification, and clustering tasks consume and produce matching paths and formats.
Acceptance Criteria: DAG imports successfully; downstream tasks wait for required upstream outputs; artifact paths match actual producers and consumers; task failures are surfaced.

Summary: Configure actionable Airflow retries and operational notifications
Description: Define bounded retry behavior for transient failures, remove placeholder notification targets, and ensure task logs report run context and failure reason.
Acceptance Criteria: Retry policy is documented and bounded; configured notification recipients come from deployment settings; a permanent error fails promptly with useful task logs.

Summary: Verify Docker local setup and service health
Description: Check MongoDB and dashboard startup, health checks, persistent data behavior, environment variable examples, and safe defaults.
Acceptance Criteria: Documented compose command starts required services; service readiness is observable; persisted catalog survives restart; example configuration contains no real secret.

Summary: Add end-to-end pipeline and dashboard smoke checks
Description: Exercise a small offline fixture through cleaning and feature generation and verify dashboard data/model fallbacks without requiring TMDB access.
Acceptance Criteria: Automated checks cover the critical pipeline handoffs and dashboard startup; checks run with documented commands; failures identify the failing boundary.

Summary: Publish setup and operational runbook
Description: Document required environment variables, data and model artifact paths, local startup, pipeline execution, test commands, recovery steps, and known limitations.
Acceptance Criteria: A new contributor can follow the instructions from a clean checkout; all documented paths and commands are verified; secret values are represented only by placeholders.

Summary: Deliver reproducible exploratory movie analytics
Description: Keep the existing catalog exploration useful and reproducible with validated charts and a documented generation workflow.
Acceptance Criteria: EDA charts can be regenerated from the current feature dataset; chart inputs handle empty and missing data; generated outputs and interpretations are documented.

Summary: Make EDA chart generation robust and reusable
Description: Validate the nine existing charts against empty, sparse, and missing-field data and ensure chart functions return figures and close resources.
Acceptance Criteria: Each chart either renders valid data or reports an actionable insufficiency; figure resources are closed after generation; chart functions do not require an interactive display.

Summary: Document EDA outputs and insights
Description: Describe the chart generation command, output directory, covered fields, and interpretation caveats for the catalog analysis.
Acceptance Criteria: Documented command generates all expected chart files; output location and field requirements are accurate; observations are not presented as causal claims.
